description: Step 1 of fz-sc8.192 (page fz-sc8.192.html v2 in the workspace root; the user chose a hash tree, unordered above 32 keys, on 2026-11-14). term_hash agrees with TermComparator equality (equal terms hash equal); atoms hash by name (a hash kept in the atom table at intern), closures by denotation, so trie order is the same on interp, run and build and across runs. The trie node is a heap object: 16-way bitmap node, 4 hash bits per level, entries inline, collision node when hash bits run out, entry count at the root; header, size, collector trace and forward under minor and major collections, deep copy and gift with shared nodes copied once. A MapLayout variant with get, has_key, count, walk, equality, compare (sorting by key when order is asked), print. Bulk builders (fz_map_from_kv, destination freeze/publish) make a trie above 32 entries; put, delete and update on a trie may rebuild in this step. Replaces the ordered-tree code (runtime/src/heap/map_tree.rs, local commit only); keeps the quoted-source reader going through the entry accessor. Signal: property tests (equal implies same hash; trie against a reference model; a key with heavily shared substructure hashes in bounded time or the cost is reported); a fixture builds a 10,000-key map in one call and reads it every way on interp, run and build against an Elixir oracle with sorted output; a census of every golden that prints a map over 32 keys; maps of 32 entries or fewer are byte-identical (no existing pin moves). Spike: worktree fz-maps-spike (runtime/src/term_hash.rs, heap/map_spike.rs), tables in scratchpad mapspike/.
title: A map built over 32 keys in one call is a hash tree that every read understands
